newsitem.title: USA: Venture sales decline narrows in January.
newsitem.headline: Venture sales decline narrows in January.

text.p: Venture Stores Inc reported its comparable store sales gap narrowed in January, the second consecutive month of improvement, and said it is a sign of progress in its strategic repositioning.
The retailer posted a comparable store sales decline in January (four weeks ending January 25, 1997) of 7.4 percent, compared with December's comparable store decrease of 13.5 percent.

"Venture closed out the 1996 fiscal year with some encouraging top line trends, as our comparable store sales gap narrowed noticeably in December and even more significantly in January, despite adverse weather conditions in most of our markets," said Robert Wildrick, chairman and chief executive officer in a statement.

He also noted sales rose 26.1 percent in December and January for new and expanded apparel, home, and leisure departments launched during the first two phases of the repositioning. As part of the third phase of its repositioning, Venture plans to open or expand 14 more departments starting in March 1997.

Venture's total sales for the four weeks ended January 25, 1997 fell 10.5 percent from the same period last year to $75.0 million. For the year-to-date 1996 sales (52 weeks ended January 25, 1997) were $1.48 billion, down 23 percent from $1.93 billion for 1995. Comparable store sales for the year declined 20.2 percent.
Venture operates 113 family value stores in nine states.
Shares of Venture were trading unchanged at 2-1/2.
